frozen_candidate_root_contribution: In its dominant lexicalized nominal shape — the faʿlah noun ḥasrah / plural ḥasarāt (9 of 12 occurrences) — the root names anguished, terminal regret felt over an irrecoverable loss or a neglected obligation: the self's grieving reaction to what can no longer be undone. It is regularly directed by ʿalā + the thing regretted (39:56 ʿalā mā farraṭtu, 6:31 ʿalā mā farraṭnā, 36:30 ʿalā l-ʿibād, 69:50 ʿalā l-kāfirīn) or seated fī qulūb (3:156), and is tied to irreversibility (19:39 the Day when qudiya l-amr; 2:167 deeds shown back with no return). It denotes neither the loss itself nor generic sorrow. This claim is scoped to that lexicalized class; a separate depletion/exhaustion class (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) is present in the root and is NOT Quran-internally bridged to it.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: For its most common form, the noun ḥasrah, this root means the bitter, too-late regret you feel over something lost or neglected that can never be put right — the anguish of 'if only,' not just sadness and not the loss itself. A separate handful of words from the same root (a worn-out eye, tireless angels, a man left destitute) instead mean being drained or worn out physically, with no regret in them at all. The Quran never uses one word that carries both meanings, so we make the confident claim only about the ḥasrah 'regret' family and record the 'depletion' words as an unbridged second class.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Hsr (the ḥasrah class) does NOT denote: (1) the loss/ruin itself — that is the near-homograph root khsr, set side by side in 6:31 (qad khasira ... qālū yā-ḥasratanā), where khasira names the loss and ḥasrah the anguished reaction to it; (2) the punishment/fire — ḥasrah in 2:167 and 8:36 is distinct from al-nār / jahannam named in the same verses; (3) corrective remorse-with-remedy — every instance is terminal (law, farraṭnā already done, wa-mā hum bi-khārijīn); (4) generic sorrow or fear (ḥuzn) — it is specifically retrospective regret over the irreversible. Separately, the depletion class does NOT entail any emotion (its subjects include the sinless angels, 21:19) and is not the same as being repelled/abased (ḥasīr is co-listed with, hence distinct from, khāsiʾ in 67:4).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 21:19:13:1 yastaḥsirūn (wa-lā yastaḥsirūn, of the angels): the one finite verb of the root, predicated of sinless beings for whom regret is impossible, negated in parallel with yastakbirūn (pride) — its sense is unmistakably 'grow weary / flag / become spent,' pure depletion of stamina with zero regret. Reinforced by 67:4 ḥasīr (the strained sight returns worn out) and 17:29 maḥsūr (one sits stripped/destitute after over-spending). These three disprove any attempt to read the whole root as 'regret' and force recognition of a depletion class that the ḥasrah-regret claim does not and should not cover.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: The unified-nucleus reading: a single root value 'worn down / spent to depletion' — of stamina (21:19), sight (67:4), means (17:29), and, in the lexicalized noun, of the heart consumed by regret (the 9 ḥasrah tokens), with 35:8 (lā tadhhab nafsuka ... ḥasarāt, grief that consumes the self) offered as the internal hinge. It is attractive because ḥasrah is a regular deverbal noun off the same root and the verbal system coheres. It is rejected as the graded claim because no single occurrence co-activates both senses: the emotional↔physical bridge is supplied by inference, and 'depletion/emptiness' is broad enough to fit almost any negative state (a fit-everything abstraction the methodology disqualifies). Even the best bridge candidate, 17:29 maḥsūr, resolves to material destitution, not anguish.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three analyses converge on a real, surface-visible two-class split with sense confounded with morphology: the 'regret' sense occurs ONLY in the frozen faʿlah noun ḥasrah/ḥasarāt (9/12), the 'depletion' sense ONLY in non-ḥasrah forms (maḥsūr participle, yastaḥsirūn Form X, ḥasīr faʿīl, 3/12). No Quranic occurrence bridges the two, so per contract the single root nucleus is left UNRESOLVED rather than forced. What IS well-supported is a narrow, distinctive account of the dominant lexicalized ḥasrah class — terminal regret over irrecoverable loss/neglect — clean within its 9 tokens and sharply distinguished from the homograph khsr (loss), from ḥuzn (generic sorrow), and from the fire/punishment. Because a coherent resistant lexicalized/nominal split exists and the cross-class bridge is not demonstrated, strength is capped at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE, with claim_scope_kind LEXICALIZED_CLASS naming the ḥasrah family the claim actually covers.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: A resource or faculty worn down / spent to the point of depletion or incapacity — of means (maḥsūr, 17:29: sitting stripped/destitute after over-spending), of stamina (yastaḥsirūn, 21:19: angels who do not flag in worship), of visual power (ḥasīr, 67:4: the strained sight returns worn out). No affective/regret content.
clusters.classification_rationale: These occupy the productive verbal/adjectival system (Form I maf‘ūl participle, Form X finite verb, faʿīl adjective) rather than the ḥasrah noun, and carry morally-neutral physical exhaustion — 21:19's subjects are the sinless angels, excluding any regret reading. They resist the ḥasrah-regret claim and are not Quran-internally bridged to it (no token co-activates both senses).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 21:19 negates the root in parallel with yastakbirūn (pride), naming stamina-failure; 67:4 co-lists ḥasīr with the distinct khāsiʾ; 17:29 co-lists maḥsūr with the distinct malūm, isolating 'depleted of means' as the root's contribution.

reconciliation.rationale: The participle is built on the depletion verb and the clause (over-spending the hand kulla l-basṭ, then sitting malūman maḥsūran) supports 'destitute/stripped,' with malūm carrying the blame separately. It does not demonstrate the affective ḥasrah sense, so it stays in the resistant depletion class rather than bridging the two classes.

The token is the ḥasrah noun and its content is regret/grief over the misguided, not physical exhaustion; the 'self expiring' is idiomatic intensity of regret. It supports the ḥasrah-regret class and does not, by itself, demonstrate a bridge to the depletion forms, so unity remains inferential and is not asserted.

adversarial_verification.notes: The ḥasrah-regret class is internally clean and distinctive (against khsr, ḥuzn, and the fire), but a coherent resistant depletion class persists at the root level and no occurrence bridges the two. Per contract, when some occurrences resist while the scoped class core holds, falsification is NOT_RUN and the resisting occurrences (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) are recorded rather than a PASSED verdict claimed.

independent_verification: All three independent analyses (A, B, adversary C) reached the same two-class split, the same unbridged status, and the same REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE grade; C additionally verified that sense is confounded with morphology so no minimal pair exists to test unity.
candidate_root_contribution: In its dominant lexicalized nominal shape — the faʿlah noun ḥasrah / plural ḥasarāt (9 of 12 occurrences) — the root names anguished, terminal regret felt over an irrecoverable loss or a neglected obligation: the self's grieving reaction to what can no longer be undone. It is regularly directed by ʿalā + the thing regretted (39:56 ʿalā mā farraṭtu, 6:31 ʿalā mā farraṭnā, 36:30 ʿalā l-ʿibād, 69:50 ʿalā l-kāfirīn) or seated fī qulūb (3:156), and is tied to irreversibility (19:39 the Day when qudiya l-amr; 2:167 deeds shown back with no return). It denotes neither the loss itself nor generic sorrow. This claim is scoped to that lexicalized class; a separate depletion/exhaustion class (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) is present in the root and is NOT Quran-internally bridged to it.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 12/12 occurrences read from the packet; 9 are the faʿlah noun ḥasrah/ḥasarāt (19:39, 2:167, 35:8, 36:30, 39:56, 3:156, 69:50, 6:31, 8:36), 3 are non-ḥasrah depletion forms — maḥsūr maf‘ūl participle (17:29), yastaḥsirūn Form X verb (21:19), ḥasīr faʿīl adjective (67:4).
layer_attribution.derivation: ḥasrah/ḥasarāt is a lexicalized faʿlah deverbal noun; the depletion sense lives in the still-productive verbal/adjectival system. Sense is confounded with morphology (regret only in the noun, depletion only in the derived forms), so no minimal pair exists to test a single nucleus.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: The graded claim is scoped to the lexicalized ḥasrah/ḥasarāt nominal class = anguished, terminal regret over an irrecoverable loss or neglected obligation.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Within that class, regret is directed by ʿalā + the regretted object (39:56, 6:31, 36:30, 69:50) or seated fī qulūb (3:156), and bound to irreversibility (19:39 qudiya l-amr; 2:167 no return from the fire; 39:56/6:31 farraṭa). This is the collocational profile of the class, not a separate root meaning imported from narrative context.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: 17:29 maḥsūr, the most ambiguous bridge candidate, resolves to resource-depletion (destitute after over-spending) and remains in the resistant class; 35:8 ḥasarāt remains regret within the ḥasrah class. No occurrence co-activates both senses, so no bridge is asserted.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The depletion class (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) is not Quran-internally bridged to the ḥasrah-regret class; the single root nucleus remains UNRESOLVED and is deliberately not forced, with 6:31 also marking the boundary against the homograph khsr (loss).

evidence_basis.statement: 21:19 yastaḥsirūn, the one finite verb of the root, predicated of angels and paired against yastakbirūn, means grow weary/flag — pure depletion of stamina with zero regret.

evidence_basis.statement: 67:4 ḥasīr names the strained sight returning worn out/spent, distinct from co-listed khāsiʾ, with no affective content.

hard_cases.reason: maḥsūr = stripped/destitute after over-spending; the most ambiguous bridge candidate, but it resolves to resource-depletion, not anguish, so the bridge is not demonstrated.

evidence_basis.statement: 17:29 maḥsūr denotes being stripped/destitute of means after over-extending in spending, with malūm (blame) a separate coordinate term; it does not co-activate the regret sense.

hard_cases.reason: In one verse yā-ḥasratanā (our root, regret) stands beside qad khasira (root khsr, loss), fixing the negative boundary that Hsr is the anguished reaction, not the loss itself.

evidence_basis.statement: 6:31 juxtaposes khasira (loss, root khsr) and yā-ḥasratanā (regret, root Hsr), showing the two homographic roots are deliberately distinct.

hard_case_representation.rationale: A coherent depletion/exhaustion class (17:29 maḥsūr, 21:19 yastaḥsirūn, 67:4 ḥasīr) persists unbridged to the dominant ḥasrah-regret class; no Quranic occurrence co-activates both senses, so the resistance is genuine and the single root nucleus is left UNRESOLVED rather than forced. 6:31 additionally marks the adversarial boundary against the homograph khsr.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A ḥasrah/ḥasarāt occurrence that denotes neutral physical or resource depletion (fatigue, spent eyesight, destitution) with no affective regret over an irrecoverable loss — which would show the lexicalized noun is not confined to terminal regret and would collapse the class toward the broader depletion nucleus.
rejection_condition.search_location: The nine ḥasrah noun tokens, especially the non-vocative predicatives 8:36:14:1, 69:50:2:2, 3:156:27:1, 2:167:17:1 and any collocation lacking the ʿalā + regretted-object frame or fī qulūb.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Read each ḥasrah clause for the regret frame (ʿalā mā farraṭa / ʿalā + party, fī qulūb, yawm al-ḥasrah tied to qudiya l-amr) and test whether a neutral-depletion reading fits without importing regret; check that the token is the ḥasrah noun and not a mis-tagged depletion form.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Exclude the near-homograph khsr (loss: 6:31 khasira) and the co-listed but distinct words malūm (17:29) and khāsiʾ (67:4); do not let a depletion-form token (maḥsūr, yastaḥsirūn, ḥasīr) be counted as ḥasrah, nor context-supplied grief be read into the root.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such a token is found, the lexicalized-class claim (terminal regret over irrecoverable loss) is falsified, the ḥasrah class dissolves into the depletion account, and the root would move toward either a single depletion nucleus or full UNRESOLVED.

reopen_conditions: If a Quranic occurrence is found where the ḥasrah/ḥasarāt noun carries physical/resource depletion (fatigue, spent eyesight, destitution), OR where a depletion form (17:29 maḥsūr, 21:19 yastaḥsirūn, 67:4 ḥasīr) carries affective regret, the two classes would bridge and the root should be reconsidered as a single depletion nucleus.

If the depletion cluster grows with new tokens showing an affective/regret component alongside exhaustion, or if a form intermediate between the faʿlah noun and the verbal system emerges, revisit the class boundary and the LEXICALIZED_CLASS scoping.
If 17:29 maḥsūr is shown Quran-internally to co-activate anguish (not just destitution), re-evaluate it as a genuine bridge rather than a resistant token.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The ḥasrah-regret class is internally clean and distinctive (against khsr, ḥuzn, and the fire), but a coherent resistant depletion class persists at the root level and no occurrence bridges the two. Per contract, when some occurrences resist while the scoped class core holds, falsification is NOT_RUN and the resisting occurrences (17:29, 21:19, 67:4) are recorded rather than a PASSED verdict claimed.
